note: A 52-page NetLogo agent-based modelling paper with eleven printed figures and ten typeset grids, of which only three figures and two tables carry a caption. The caption set is two grammars: sentences prefixed 'Figure N:' below the figure, and the bare words 'Table 1' and 'Table 2' above the grid. Every grid is boxed with verticals at every cell boundary, none is shaded, and only the four-column maternity/paternity grid merges cells or carries two header rows. Six grids are announced by deixis on their own page; two are read from below; Tables 1 and 2 are announced on p7 and print seventeen pages later in the appendix. The p16 pair and the p20 triple are measured as separate regions of one figure each, so two doc_orders repeat across panels and neither set shares a scale. Two figures are pasted screen captures with interface furniture printed inside them. The cover letter's p2 histogram is the paper's only wholly uncited exhibit, and the education-metric line on p21 is cited by caption alone.
rules: Twelve of the twenty-one exhibits print with caption_source 'none': four figures (p2, the p10 world series, p11, p12) and eight of the ten grids (pp8, 9, 11, 17, 18 and both grids on p19) [caption.verbatim].

The two caption grammars do not mix: every figure caption that prints is a sentence with a 'Figure N:' prefix, and the two table captions are the bare words 'Table 1' and 'Table 2' with no colon and no text [caption.numbering].
Figure captions print below their exhibit and the two table captions print above theirs, so the side is set by exhibit type in this paper rather than by chapter [caption.position].
No caption in the paper names a unit, a condition or a parameter, and only Figure 4 states anything a reader could act on ('Notice the sudden drop then spike') [caption.concludes].
Captions are short: the three numbered figure captions run 8 to 13 words, the two p16 panel captions are 5 and 7 words, and each table caption is the two-word label alone [caption.words].

The p16 pair and the p20 triple are each one figure split into separately measured regions, so both items in a pair and all three items in a triple repeat a doc_order and carry is_panel_of [place.doc_order].

Neither set of panels shares a scale: the p16 pair is drawn on independent y maxima, and the p20 triple runs 200 / 205 / 246, so no figure in the paper is readable across its panels without reading the ticks [geometry.shared_axes].

Six of the eleven figures are ggplot output - the six histograms - and all six print tick labels and nothing else. No figure in the paper prints a data label on a mark: charts are read off axes, never off labels [geometry.data_labels].
No figure is three-dimensional, no figure carries a colourbar, and the only legend in the paper is the country chip baked into the Gapminder screenshot on p10 [geometry.legend].

Two figures are screen captures rather than plots: the p10 world inflation series has a browser country selector and time scrubber printed inside it, and the p11 Canadian series prints bare two-digit year ticks (95 to 15). Both are recorded by what they show, not by how they were made [geometry.family].

Every one of the ten grids is boxed: a rule at the top, a rule under the header, rules between body rows and verticals at every cell boundary. The paper contains no booktabs grid and no rules-only grid [table.rule_style].
No grid is shaded - there is no zebra striping and no tinted cell in the paper, including the 22-row appendix tables where striping would have helped [table.zebra].
Only the maternity/paternity grid merges cells, and it is also the only grid with two header rows: each leave type spans the two columns beneath it [table.merged_cells].

Grid width tracks column count and cell text, not importance: the two 22-row appendix tables and the six-row sensitivity grid are full width because their cells wrap to several lines, the four-column leave grid is full width, and the four two- and three-column result grids stay in the column [table.width].
The two result grids on p19 are one argument split into two blocks: the tax/investment grid starts at a tax rate of 35 because that is where the row range it continues begins [table.rows].

Three of the ten grids are decimal-aligned - the education table (two decimals), the leave table (three decimals) and Table 1 (four decimals) - and the other seven hold integers or algebra and are not [table.decimal_aligned].

Six grids are announced by a deictic sentence on their own page and cited by nothing else - 'the following are the tax brackets', 'This relationship is described as follows:', 'as seen in Figure 2a.' - with no figure or table number in the announcing sentence [mention.style].
Two grids are cited from below only ('In the table above, we see ...'), so the sentence that reads the grid comes after it and the sentence that announces it does not exist [mention.trail_sentence].

Tables 1 and 2 are announced on p7 and print on pp24 and 25, a seventeen-page lead, because the announcing sentence sends the reader to the appendix rather than promising a nearby float [mention.lead_pages].

Two exhibits are never cited at all - the cover-letter histogram on p2 and the education-metric line on p21, which is named by its caption alone - and every other exhibit is mentioned exactly once [mention.count].

Exhibit size tracks nothing: the largest figure is the life-cycle flowchart at 0.285 of its page and the smallest is Figure 4 at 0.020, but the paper's headline comparison is carried by a 0.046 grid [place.area_frac].

Section kinds follow the paper's own shape: the model chapter holds six figures and five grids, the results chapter five figures and four grids, sensitivity one grid, and the appendix the two 22-row tables [place.section_kind].
